verdict_reason: I withdraw my own prior objection to the whitespace word denominator: Ali et al. (arXiv:2310.08754 v3, Sec. 3.4) define fertility as 'the number of tokens in A (when T is applied) divided by the number of words in A' and state explicitly 'For calculating the words of a document, we used whitespace splitting'. BLME computes total_tokens / len(text.split()) micro-averaged over the corpus with add_special_tokens=False -- that is the cited definition, not a proxy for it. I also fetched Rust et al.'s released tokenization_metrics/tokenizer_exploration_utils.py: their fertility is np.mean(split_lengths), the mean of per-word token counts, which is algebraically the same micro-average; the only difference from BLME is that their words come from UD/CoNLL columns rather than whitespace, worth a measured +3.5% on WikiText-103 for every one of six tokenizers. compression_ratio, token_entropy and vocab_utilization compute exactly what the module docstring says they compute.
comparable_reason: Three of the emitted keys are one measurement. On the shipped built-in corpus (the default when no dataset is passed) total_words and total_chars are the same constants for every model, so fertility, compression_ratio and total_tokens are exact rescalings of each other: Pearson r = 1.0000000000 for both pairs across gpt2, pythia-160m, opt-125m, Qwen2.5-0.5B, Llama-3.2-1B and phi-1_5. Five of those six tokenizers return the identical fertility 1.1845 on that corpus, i.e. essentially zero discrimination. The two vocabulary-normalised keys are vocabulary-size readouts: r(normalised_token_entropy, 1/log V) = 0.9996 and r(vocab_utilization, 1/V) = 0.9998.
github_reason: Fetched Rust et al.'s released tokenization-metrics utility and read the fertility computation: per-word token counts are accumulated in split_lengths over UD/CoNLL word columns and reported as np.mean(split_lengths), which equals total_tokens/total_words. I could not RUN it head-to-head because the repo ships no UD v2.6 treebanks (only reduced mBERT vocabularies), so there is no same-input numeric comparison. Ali et al. released no tokenizer-metric code I could locate; their fertility comes from an unreleased 10,000-document held-out set.
paper_reason: Neither source publishes a number this task can be pointed at. Rust et al. report fertility only as bars in a per-language figure over UD v2.6 treebanks that are not bundled; Ali et al. plot fertility curves for tokenizers they trained themselves on an unreleased 10,000-document sample and tabulate no coordinates. For orientation only (not a reproduction): BLME's gpt2 whitespace fertility on 1,000 WikiText-103 documents is 1.1770, inside the band Ali et al.'s Fig. 1(b) shows for English tokenizers on English text.
confounds_reason: vocab_size is emitted as a first-class feature, and two more keys are monotone functions of it (r = 0.9996 with 1/log V, r = 0.9998 with 1/V measured over six tokenizers). fertility itself is a genuine tokenizer property rather than a size proxy -- on WikiText-103 it separates tokenizers with very different vocabularies only mildly (gpt2 1.1770 at V=50257 vs Qwen2.5 1.2273 at V=151643), i.e. it does not simply track V -- but the surrounding keys do, and this task's own docstring lists vocab_size among the study's top-25 partial predictors.
defects: CONFIG: defaults.yaml sets num_samples: 20, against Ali et al.'s 10,000 held-out documents. Magnitude depends entirely on what a document is, which the config does not pin: on WikiText-103 *pages* (mean 17k chars) 20 vs 1000 documents moves fertility by only -0.17% (gpt2) to +1.13% (Qwen2.5), but on the built-in 20-sentence corpus the entire measurement is 206 words and 244 tokens.

The shipped fallback corpus is 20 hand-written English sentences. On it, five of six tokenizers report the identical fertility 1.1845 and identical compression_ratio 0.1776; the metric cannot distinguish tokenizers it is meant to rank.

CODE (non-fidelity): normalised_token_entropy divides by log(vocab_size) although a sample of T tokens cannot exceed log(min(T, V)). On the built-in corpus T = 244, so the divisor log(50257) = 10.82 is 1.97x the attainable maximum log(244) = 5.50 and the field is capped at 0.508 by construction.

CODE (non-fidelity): vocab_size uses tokenizer.vocab_size, which excludes added tokens, so the emitted vocabulary and the entropy/utilisation denominators are wrong for tokenizers that have them -- pythia-160m 50254 vs len(tokenizer) 50277, Llama-3.2-1B 128000 vs 128256 (+0.200%), phi-1_5 50257 vs 50295, Qwen2.5 151643 vs 151665. Measured production effect is small (<= 0.2%), but the same defect lets the two 'fractions' exceed 1 for any tokenizer whose observed ids run past the declared vocab.

CODE (latent): fertility = total_tokens / max(1, total_words) fabricates a finite value for text with tokens but no whitespace words (three spaces, unsegmented CJK) instead of returning NA. Does not fire on the English corpora in use.
CODE (minor): the dataset branch calls list(dataset) BEFORE applying num_samples, materialising an entire streaming/unbounded iterable to keep 20 rows; itertools.islice would bound it.
The docstring calls compression_ratio 'tokens per UTF-8 character' but len(text) counts Unicode code points, not UTF-8 bytes -- identical for ASCII, different for any non-Latin corpus.
Rust et al.'s second metric (proportion of continued words, present in their released utility) and Ali et al.'s parity are not implemented, so the two citations support one of the six outputs.
fix: 1) Raise num_samples to a versioned held-out corpus of at least a few thousand documents and pin what a document is, or publish a convergence curve; the current 20 is defensible on WikiText pages (<= 1.1% drift) and indefensible on the 206-word built-in corpus. 2) Replace tokenizer.vocab_size with len(tokenizer) (or a validated usable-id count) for the emitted vocab_size and both normalisation denominators, and assert the two fractions lie in [0,1]. 3) Either normalise token_entropy by log(min(T, V)) or rename it; as shipped it is 1/log(V) in disguise. 4) Demote compression_ratio and total_tokens to _meta_ (at fixed corpus they are fertility times a constant, r = 1.0000000000) and record the trio in the duplicate table. 5) Return NA when total_words is 0 instead of dividing by 1, and slice the dataset lazily.
fix_applied: R27: replaced tokenizer.vocab_size with len(tokenizer) for the emitted vocab_size and both normalisation denominators -- vocab_size is the BASE vocabulary and excludes added/special tokens, so pythia-70m reports 50277 against a base of 50254 and both fractions could leave [0,1]. normalised_token_entropy now divides by log(min(T,V)) rather than log(V): an empirical entropy over T tokens cannot exceed log(T), so the old ceiling was unreachable and model-dependent (at T=10k, V=50k the max attainable is 0.851). Realised ceiling emitted as _meta_entropy_ceiling_n; both fractions clamped and asserted in [0,1].
